svg.title: For each fixed stage the startup threshold is finite. Include it in the same entry-delay maximum. At level zero the calendar identifies the initial stage with its first entry stage, so this threshold is paid there too; at a successor level it follows from the previous entry payment and the positive coupling increment. Consequently the chosen calendar gives (CAL21) at every possible finest cutoff. For any actual coupling in [x/2, 2x], the startup expansion is still valid: its lower-coupling hypothesis follows from the left endpoint, and its vacuum price is bounded using the right endpoint. The exact startup density identity then turns (CAL21) into the required forced-activity bound. These choices enlarge delays before the final calendar and history are selected, and preserve all earlier purchases. They add no assumption to the theorem.
